source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
One campus, CyrusOne's PNW1 in Quincy, accounts for 60 percent of Washington's publicly declared data center IT load, because only 2 of the state's 46 mapped facilities disclose capacity at all.

That 60 percent measures disclosure, not load. The 36 MW figure is specific to this campus, but the state total it is measured against is a partial record, so the true share of this site within Washington's data center footprint is unknown. The gap between 46 mapped facilities and 2 with published power specifications is the more informative number here.

For AI, the binding number is megawatts delivered to racks. The campus holds 36 MW of IT capacity across 720,000 square feet of technical space, about 50 watts per square foot, and at an assumed 40 kW per rack that is roughly 900 racks. That intensity is consistent with high-density compute, but the published specifications do not identify tenants or workload type, so nothing in this data establishes that the capacity serves AI training rather than any other load.

What the record does not cover is whether the 36 MW is being drawn today or held as headroom, whether the grid connection can support expansion, and whether the operator has filed for capacity beyond what is disclosed. No certifications or utility partnership details are published. The suitability score of 68 is built only from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing, so it describes what is on the record rather than what the site can do.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
